mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-01.stem: If rolling achieves the required thickness, all later property adjustment and surface treatment become unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Achieving the required thickness differs from achieving hardness, surface condition and other properties. Check the process sheet for required heat treatment, surface treatment and inspections.

False. Achieving the required thickness differs from achieving hardness, surface condition and other properties. Check the process sheet for required heat treatment, surface treatment and inspections.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-02.stem: Pull a person suspected of receiving an electric shock directly by hand before checking the power supply.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Direct contact may also give the rescuer an electric shock. Do not contact potentially energized parts; report and perform any safely possible stopping from a safe position.
False. Direct contact may also give the rescuer an electric shock. Do not contact potentially energized parts; report and perform any safely possible stopping from a safe position.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-03.stem: A motor converts electrical energy to mechanical power, driving conveyors, pumps and other equipment.
reasons: True. A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical power to drive conveyors, pumps and similar equipment. A transformer changes voltage in suitable AC circuits and related applications. Neither is suitable for use merely because wires can be connected; check ratings and equipment requirements.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical power to drive conveyors, pumps and similar equipment. A transformer changes voltage in suitable AC circuits and related applications. Neither is suitable for use merely because wires can be connected; check ratings and equipment requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-04.stem: Elongation at any one point under load is invariably the same as elongation after fracture.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Elongation at a point under load and elongation after fracture are evaluated at different times and states.
False. Elongation at a point under load and elongation after fracture are evaluated at different times and states.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-05.stem: A breaker that trips repeatedly may simply be reset repeatedly even before the cause is verified.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Repeated resetting without knowing the cause reenergizes an abnormal condition. Report the situation and have the cause and safety checked.
False. Repeated resetting without knowing the cause reenergizes an abnormal condition. Report the situation and have the cause and safety checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-06.stem: A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece and applies a tool to machine its outside diameter and other features.
reasons: True. Cutting removes material with a tool to form the required shape. A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece against a tool to machine features such as outside diameters. A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative movement between tool and workpiece to produce flats and grooves. A drill press rotates a drill to make holes. Distinguishing what rotates helps explain machine roles and danger areas.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Cutting removes material with a tool to form the required shape. A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece against a tool to machine features such as outside diameters. A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative movement between tool and workpiece to produce flats and grooves. A drill press rotates a drill to make holes. Distinguishing what rotates helps explain machine roles and danger areas.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-07.stem: Increasing billet temperature without an upper limit prevents surface cracks.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Excessive temperature can also cause surface cracks and other problems. Keep within the specified range in combination with material, shape and speed.
False. Excessive temperature can also cause surface cracks and other problems. Keep within the specified range in combination with material, shape and speed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-08.stem: Do not judge heavy-load handling safety only by whether the waist is bent; also check specified aids and methods involving multiple people.
reasons: True. For heavy objects, check weight, shape, gripping points, distance and route. Safety is not decided only by whether someone bends at the waist; ask about specified aids or team-handling methods. Do not force yourself to carry an unmanageable weight. Keep away from suspended loads and restricted areas.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. For heavy objects, check weight, shape, gripping points, distance and route. Safety is not decided only by whether someone bends at the waist; ask about specified aids or team-handling methods. Do not force yourself to carry an unmanageable weight. Keep away from suspended loads and restricted areas.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-09.stem: Do not assume that experience in one process grants authority for all work; check the work assigned at your placement and required training.
reasons: True. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-10.stem: The area under a suspended load is a safe route that may be used briefly.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The risk of a falling suspended load remains even for a brief time. Follow access controls and use another safe route.
False. The risk of a falling suspended load remains even for a brief time. Follow access controls and use another safe route.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-11.stem: Gauge blocks use the distance between two specified precision measuring faces as a length reference; dirty paper between them is not proper wringing.
reasons: True. Reference length is defined between the measuring faces; foreign matter compromises proper wringing and combined length.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Adding lengths with paper or dirt present differs from wringing precision faces together, so the statement is not false.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-12.stem: If the front color is uniform, uncoated areas on required surfaces also pass corrosion-protection requirements.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Corrosion protection requires coating on the specified target surfaces. The front’s appearance does not make an uncoated back surface acceptable.
False. Corrosion protection requires coating on the specified target surfaces. The front’s appearance does not make an uncoated back surface acceptable.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-13.stem: The material describes ordinary fires involving wood or paper, oil fires, and electrical fires as A, B and C respectively.
reasons: True. The source describes ordinary fires involving wood or paper, oil fires and electrical fires as classes A, B and C. Applying water to oil or energized parts is dangerous. Read the extinguisher’s suitability marking rather than assuming every extinguishing agent suits every fire.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source describes ordinary fires involving wood or paper, oil fires and electrical fires as classes A, B and C. Applying water to oil or energized parts is dangerous. Read the extinguisher’s suitability marking rather than assuming every extinguishing agent suits every fire.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-14.stem: A QC circle can prove the cause of equipment defects solely by majority vote.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Majority voting can select an opinion but does not prove a cause as fact. Investigate departmental data and the actual condition.
False. Majority voting can select an opinion but does not prove a cause as fact. Investigate departmental data and the actual condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-15.stem: Longitudinal streaks on extruded products cannot possibly have any cause other than the die.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Foreign matter or contact on the runout support, as well as the die, can cause longitudinal streaks. Cross-check their location and continuity against the process.
False. Foreign matter or contact on the runout support, as well as the die, can cause longitudinal streaks. Cross-check their location and continuity against the process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-16.stem: Work standards clarify work content, sequence, equipment, tools, important conditions and other matters to maintain required quality despite changes in personnel or time.
reasons: True. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-17.stem: Even with tool outlines indicating locations, returning a tool of a different size does not maintain the fixed-item principle.
reasons:
True. The three fixed conditions make the location, type, and quantity of items explicit. Fixed location specifies where to put them, fixed item specifies what to put there, and fixed quantity specifies how much to keep. Combining all three makes shortages and mixed items easier to detect.
Even if a tool outline marks its place, returning a different size of tool fails the fixed-item rule. Likewise, placing the correct parts on the correct shelf but stacking them beyond the limit can make retrieval difficult and lead to toppling or falling items.
More stock does not automatically mean greater reassurance. Set the amount according to the process requirement, replenishment timing, and storage method. Sharing how to report and replenish when stock falls below the lower limit makes the system easier to operate when staff change.
If you cannot read a location or item label, do not replenish parts based only on their appearance. Check the label and instructions; place unidentified items separately in the designated area and ask for advice.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The three fixed conditions make the location, type, and quantity of items explicit. Fixed location specifies where to put them, fixed item specifies what to put there, and fixed quantity specifies how much to keep. Combining all three makes shortages and mixed items easier to detect.
Even if a tool outline marks its place, returning a different size of tool fails the fixed-item rule. Likewise, placing the correct parts on the correct shelf but stacking them beyond the limit can make retrieval difficult and lead to toppling or falling items.
More stock does not automatically mean greater reassurance. Set the amount according to the process requirement, replenishment timing, and storage method. Sharing how to report and replenish when stock falls below the lower limit makes the system easier to operate when staff change.
If you cannot read a location or item label, do not replenish parts based only on their appearance. Check the label and instructions; place unidentified items separately in the designated area and ask for advice.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-18.stem: A dust mask protects against all unknown harmful gases and oxygen deficiency.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Dust masks protect against particles, not every gas or oxygen deficiency. Check the target hazard and equipment conditions.
False. Dust masks protect against particles, not every gas or oxygen deficiency. Check the target hazard and equipment conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-19.stem: The harder a caliper is squeezed, the more accurate it invariably becomes.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Excessive force can cause deformation or poor contact. Follow the correct measuring faces, orientation, contact and specified method.
False. Excessive force can cause deformation or poor contact. Follow the correct measuring faces, orientation, contact and specified method.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-20.stem: When considering risk, examine not only the presence of hazards but also accident severity, likelihood, opportunities for exposure and other factors.
reasons:
True. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
First consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or reduced. If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
First consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or reduced. If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-21.stem: Increasing drawing-paper size automatically makes its content accurate.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Paper size does not automatically change content accuracy. Check the appropriate drawing, readability and instructions.
False. Paper size does not automatically change content accuracy. Check the appropriate drawing, readability and instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-22.stem: Rockwell uses indentation depth, Brinell indentation diameter, and Vickers diagonal length, among other distinctions.
reasons: True. Hardness testing evaluates another property. Rockwell uses indentation depth, Brinell uses indentation diameter, and Vickers uses diagonal length. HRC, HBW, and HV relate to test methods and conditions, rather than being decorative labels. Do not extract only the number and compare different methods as though they share one scale; assess using the specified method and conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Hardness testing evaluates another property. Rockwell uses indentation depth, Brinell uses indentation diameter, and Vickers uses diagonal length. HRC, HBW, and HV relate to test methods and conditions, rather than being decorative labels. Do not extract only the number and compare different methods as though they share one scale; assess using the specified method and conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-23.stem: Once a mold opens, the product is invariably at a touch-safe temperature and fully cured.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An open mold does not guarantee completed cooling or curing. Check specified conditions for removal, cooling and inspection.
False. An open mold does not guarantee completed cooling or curing. Check specified conditions for removal, cooling and inspection.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-24.stem: Read reference positions indicated by thin two-dot chain phantom lines separately from the current component’s finished outline.
reasons: True. Phantom lines can show adjacent components or movement positions for reference; do not replace every such line with the actual object’s outline.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Reading a reference shape as an instruction to remove material to that shape misunderstands the line type’s role; distinguishing it is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-25.stem: At the same applied voltage, a greater resistance gives a smaller current.
reasons: True. Voltage is measured in V, current in A, and resistance in Ω. Under applicable conditions, the voltage across a resistor and its current obey V = I × R. With the same voltage across a fixed resistor, a larger resistance gives a smaller current. This does not mean that an entire machine may always be calculated as a single resistor.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Voltage is measured in V, current in A, and resistance in Ω. Under applicable conditions, the voltage across a resistor and its current obey V = I × R. With the same voltage across a fixed resistor, a larger resistance gives a smaller current. This does not mean that an entire machine may always be calculated as a single resistor.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-26.stem: A lower-density material is invariably better for every application.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Weight reduction from low density and suitability for an application are different matters. Also check strength, deformation, temperature, geometry and other factors.
False. Weight reduction from low density and suitability for an application are different matters. Also check strength, deformation, temperature, geometry and other factors.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-27.stem: In representative steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness and other properties after quenching.
reasons: True. Heat treatment changes metal structure and properties through heating and cooling conditions. In typical steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness, and other properties after quenching. Annealing may soften the material to improve machinability. Not every metal hardens in the same way under identical heating and cooling.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Heat treatment changes metal structure and properties through heating and cooling conditions. In typical steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness, and other properties after quenching. Annealing may soften the material to improve machinability. Not every metal hardens in the same way under identical heating and cooling.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-28.stem: If the voltage number matches, there is no need to check AC/DC type or frequency.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even at the same voltage, differences in AC/DC type, frequency or ratings may make a supply incompatible. Check the nameplate and specified supply.
False. Even at the same voltage, differences in AC/DC type, frequency or ratings may make a supply incompatible. Check the nameplate and specified supply.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-29.stem: Reduce means reducing waste generation; reuse means using items repeatedly; recycle means utilizing waste as a resource.
reasons: True. Reduce prevents waste generation, reuse uses an item repeatedly, and recycle uses waste as a resource. These are not different names for the same task. Reducing unnecessary packaging and collecting used packaging to turn it back into material act at different stages.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Reduce prevents waste generation, reuse uses an item repeatedly, and recycle uses waste as a resource. These are not different names for the same task. Reducing unnecessary packaging and collecting used packaging to turn it back into material act at different stages.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-theory-30.stem: Brush painting spreads paint with a tool, while spray painting atomizes and sprays the paint.
reasons: True. Coating does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and can provide functions such as insulation or heat shielding. Brush coating spreads paint with a tool; spray coating atomizes it onto the surface. Electrostatic coating uses forces from electric charge, while electrodeposition forms a film electrically in a bath. Similar names do not mean identical processes.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Coating does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and can provide functions such as insulation or heat shielding. Brush coating spreads paint with a tool; spray coating atomizes it onto the surface. Electrostatic coating uses forces from electric charge, while electrodeposition forms a film electrically in a bath. Similar names do not mean identical processes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-01.stem: Choose a countermeasure for a passage where a load obstructs visibility. Which is most specific?
options: Only resolve to be more careful.
Check stacking and travel paths and define designated stopping-and-checking points.
Drive faster to shorten crossing time.
reasons: Resolve alone does not change why the load obstructs visibility or the checking actions.
Do not reproduce an actual dangerous transport operation for KYT.
Check causes such as stacking and travel paths and specifically decide where to stop and check.
Increasing travel speed can make stopping and checking for pedestrians more difficult.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-02.stem: In a paper example, a force of 9000 N acts on an original cross-sectional area of 30 mm². What is nominal stress?
reasons: 9000 ÷ 30 = 300; 30 N/mm² is one tenth of this.
9000 × 30 is the product of force and area, not the division required for nominal stress.
Nominal stress is force ÷ original cross-sectional area, so 9000 ÷ 30 = 300 N/mm².
3 N/mm² is one hundredth of the correct 300 N/mm².

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-03.stem: You are planning processes for a component with an outside diameter, a flat surface and a hole. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Declare that a round-bar material means everything must use only a lathe.
Organize candidate machine roles and verify them against the drawing, capabilities and approved process.
Treat everything as casting because there is a hole.
Choose the process solely by tool color.
reasons: Round-bar stock geometry alone does not determine how flats and holes will be machined.
Organize candidates such as turning, milling and drilling and verify applicability against the drawing, capability and approved process.
A hole alone does not justify choosing casting; check requirements and equipment conditions.
Tool color does not verify the shape-forming principle or equipment capability.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-04.stem: An extruded product has continuous scratches at the same position. Which investigation plan is appropriate?
options: The die is invariably the only cause.
Consider the die, runout supports and travel route as checks, and record facts.
Stop the moving product by hand to inspect it.
reasons: Contact or foreign matter during handling, as well as the die, may cause scratches.
Record scratch position and continuity, and safely investigate the die, supports and travel route.
Stopping a moving product by hand creates contact, entanglement and other hazards.
Excessive temperature can also cause surface cracks and other problems; do not maximize it unconditionally.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-05.stem: All unhatched areas on a sectional view were treated as cavities. What review is needed?
options: No hatching always means air, so leave it.
Treat all hatching as machined grooves.
Cut the actual object before considering it.
Consider features left unsectioned and compare other views and the cutting position.
reasons: Some features are left unsectioned; absence of hatching alone does not prove a cavity.
Hatching represents a cut surface, not an instruction to machine diagonal grooves.
A sectional view is an imaginary representation, not an instruction to cut the actual object.
Read the cutting position, relevant components and features left unsectioned together with other views.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-06.stem: Near misses at the same location have increased this month. What is needed after compiling counts?
options: Wait until the numbers match the ratio.
Proceed with specific facts, countermeasures and effectiveness checks.
Treat the count table alone as completion of all measures.
reasons: Heinrich’s ratio is not a count threshold for waiting before responding.
Organize possible causes from the location, actions and conditions, and check effects after implementing measures.
Reports without injury can also reveal signs of danger; do not discard them.
Compiling counts alone does not constitute addressing causes or checking effectiveness.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-07.stem: You want to replace a breaker with a higher-rated one without authorization after an overcurrent trip. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: Do not replace it; ask the responsible person to verify the cause and required ratings.
A larger rating is safer for every facility.
Disable protective action because it is a nuisance.
Repeated resets make the cause disappear.
reasons: Check the cause and required ratings; do not change protection conditions without authorization.
A higher rating can compromise specified protection and is not safe for every facility.
Disabling protection prevents interruption of dangerous overcurrent.
Repeated resets do not necessarily remove the cause; reenergizing can spread hazards.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-08.stem: A caliper reads in 0.02 mm increments; the main scale is 21 mm and the eighth vernier line aligns. What is the value?
reasons: This treats the eighth line as 0.08 mm and does not use the specified 0.02 mm increment.
This treats the eighth line as 0.80 mm, differing from 0.02 × 8 = 0.16 mm.
This adds line number 8 directly to main-scale value 21, ignoring the quantity represented by each graduation.
Add the vernier contribution 8 × 0.02 = 0.16 mm to the main scale 21 mm to obtain 21.16 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-09.stem: One product has 3 scratches and another has 1 scratch. What is the number of nonconforming products?
reasons: Count the two products bearing scratches, not the total of four scratches, so the answer is 2 items.
4 is the number of scratches, not the number of nonconforming products.
Two products have scratches, so it is not 1 item.
This confuses the first product’s three scratches with the product count.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-05-practical-10.stem: A reaction accepting electrons and a pH decrease were described as the same thing. Which correction is appropriate?
options: Distinguish electron acceptance as reduction and pH as an indicator of acidity and related properties.
Electrons and pH always have the same value.
No visible change means no reaction.
reasons: Electron acceptance is reduction, while pH indicates acidity or alkalinity of an aqueous solution; they are different perspectives.
Calling electron acceptance oxidation reverses the relationship.
Electron transfer and pH are not the same numerical quantity and cannot be directly equated.
Some reactions produce no visible change, so appearance alone cannot establish the absence of a reaction.
